event.karoo_stagnant_water.body: The only water for miles is a pool of still, green water in a hollow. The oxen are already pulling toward it. {speaker} looks at it doubtfully.
event.karoo_stagnant_water.drink: Let everyone drink and fill the vats
event.karoo_stagnant_water.drink.ok: The water tastes of mud, but it does no harm.
event.karoo_stagnant_water.drink.sick: By evening there is trouble: the bad water has made people ill.
event.karoo_stagnant_water.boil: Boil the water before anyone drinks (half a day)
event.karoo_stagnant_water.boil.ok: It takes a long time and much fuel, but the water is safe.
event.karoo_stagnant_water.push_on: Push on to find better water
event.karoo_stagnant_water.push_on.done: You drive the thirsty oxen past the pool. They low miserably all afternoon.
event.karoo_stagnant_water.ask.spring: {speaker} leads you to a spring under a rocky ridge, clear and cold. The oxen drink their fill.
event.karoo_stagnant_water.ask.none: {speaker} searches the hollows for hours but finds nothing better.
event.oxen_stray.body: At first light the oxen are gone. {speaker} finds their tracks leading away into the veld; they must have smelt good grass somewhere in the night.
event.oxen_stray.track: Follow the tracks at once (half a day)
event.oxen_stray.track.found: The spoor leads to a green valley, and there are the oxen, grazing as though nothing had happened.
event.oxen_stray.track.lost: You find most of them, but two oxen are never seen again.
event.oxen_stray.wait: Wait for them to wander back
event.oxen_stray.wait.back: Late the next day the oxen come straggling back on their own.
event.oxen_stray.wait.lost: Some come back. Three do not.
event.horses_go_home.body: In the night two of the horses have broken their riems and gone. They were bred in this district, and the men think they have gone back to their old grazing.
event.horses_go_home.send: Send a rider back to look for them (a day)
event.horses_go_home.send.found: The horses are found where everyone guessed, at their old farm.
event.horses_go_home.send.lost: The rider comes back empty-handed. The horses are gone.
event.horses_go_home.let_go: Let them go; you cannot spare the time
event.wagon_hole.body: Without warning, the wagon drops into a deep hole beside the track and tips over on its side. Boxes, pots and bedding spill into the grass.
event.wagon_hole.unload: Unload everything and right the wagon carefully (a day)
event.wagon_hole.unload.done: It takes all day. The wagon tent is torn, but nothing else is broken.
event.wagon_hole.pull: Hitch the oxen and drag it upright
event.wagon_hole.pull.ok: With a great heave the wagon comes upright. The tent is torn, but the wheels are sound.
event.wagon_hole.pull.bad: The wagon comes up, but a wheel is badly cracked in the process.
event.quicksand.body: Crossing a stream, a horse suddenly sinks to its belly in quicksand and begins to struggle.
event.quicksand.riems: Throw riems around it and haul it out
event.quicksand.riems.ok: Everyone heaves on the riems, and the horse comes out with a great sucking sound, muddy but unhurt.
event.quicksand.riems.lost: You try for an hour, but the sand will not give it up.
event.mirage.body: Ahead, the plain shines with water: a wide lake, its surface rippling in the heat. The thirsty oxen have seen it too, and they start to run.
event.mirage.hold.ok: The herders hold them, and as you come closer the 'lake' turns into a crust of white salt on the ground.
event.mirage.hold.bad: The oxen break away and run until they find only salt. They come back exhausted.
event.mirage.let: Let them run; perhaps it is real
event.mirage.let.done: There is no water, only a shimmer of heat over white salt. The oxen are worn out for nothing.
event.dogs_paws.body: The ground is so hot that the dogs' paws are burned raw. They limp along behind the wagon, whining.
event.dogs_paws.grease: Treat their paws with tallow and axle grease
event.dogs_paws.grease.done: The dogs soon learn what the grease pot is for. Before long they come up holding out a paw for more, which makes the children laugh.
event.dogs_paws.carry: Let the dogs ride in the wagon
event.dogs_paws.carry.done: The dogs ride on the load like lords, looking down at everyone walking.
event.hyenas_night.body: In the dark something is moving around the wagons. Hyenas, drawn by the smell of meat, are creeping close to the fire.
event.hyenas_night.shot: Fire a shot into the dark
event.hyenas_night.shot.done: The shot echoes across the veld, and the hyenas scatter howling.
event.hyenas_night.fire: Build up the fire and keep watch
event.hyenas_night.fire.ok: The bright fire keeps them off until dawn.
event.hyenas_night.fire.bad: In the grey before dawn they dart in and run off with meat from the wagon.
event.storm_cattle.body: A storm breaks in the night. The wind thrashes the reeds and thunder rolls overhead. The cattle panic and break loose, again and again. {speaker} is already running for the herd.
event.storm_cattle.chase: Go after them in the dark
event.storm_cattle.chase.ok: Soaked and bruised, {speaker} and the others drive the herd back into the lee of the wagons.
event.storm_cattle.chase.lost: You catch most of them, but some are lost in the storm.
event.storm_cattle.wait: Stay by the wagons until it passes
event.storm_cattle.wait.done: In the morning the cattle are scattered over miles of veld. Not all of them can be found.
event.quagga_sunrise.body: At sunrise a troop of quaggas grazes near the camp, with foals among them. They are striped like zebras at the front but plain brown behind.
event.quagga_sunrise.watch.done: The children watch until the herd moves off over the rise. It is a sight they will remember all their lives.
event.lions_herd.body: A deep roar comes out of the darkness, close by. The oxen bellow and strain at their riems. Lions are prowling around the herd.
event.lions_herd.fire_guns: Fire the guns to drive them off
event.lions_herd.fire_guns.ok: The volley echoes through the night. The roaring moves away.
event.lions_herd.fire_guns.bad: The lions run, but in the confusion one ox is pulled down in the dark.
event.lions_herd.fires: Light fires all around the herd
event.lions_herd.fires.ok: No one sleeps, but the fires keep the lions away.
event.lions_herd.fires.bad: The fires burn low before dawn, and a cow is taken.
event.servant_wages.body: {speaker} comes to speak with you. "Baas, men are paid more than this on the farms in the Colony. I have family to think of."
event.servant_wages.body@english: {speaker} comes to speak with you. "Sir, men are paid more than this on the farms in the Colony. I have family to think of."
event.servant_wages.raise: Raise the wage (a month's extra pay now)
event.servant_wages.raise.done: {speaker} thanks you. The work goes better after that.
event.servant_wages.promise: Promise more when you reach the next town
event.servant_wages.promise.done: {speaker} nods, but you can see the promise will need keeping.
event.servant_wages.refuse.done: {speaker} says nothing more, but works in silence from then on.
event.smous_visit.body: A smous comes along the track with a wagon full of goods: coffee, sugar, cloth, buttons, needles and medicines. He has news from every farm between here and Graaff-Reinet.
event.smous_visit.coffee: Buy coffee and sugar (6 lb each)
event.smous_visit.coffee.done: The price is high, as a smous's prices always are, but tonight there will be coffee.
event.smous_visit.medicine.done: He sells you a few bottles of Dutch remedies with great praise for each of them.
event.smous_visit.news.done: He talks for an hour about who is trekking, who is staying, and what everything costs.
event.child_wanders.body: At the midday halt someone notices that a child is missing. Nobody has seen them for an hour.
event.child_wanders.search.found: The child is found asleep under a bush, quite unaware of the fuss.
event.child_wanders.search.night: The search goes on until dark. At last the child is found, cold and frightened, but alive.
event.snakebite.body: A scream from the long grass: someone has been bitten by a snake.
event.snakebite.treat: Treat the bite with medicine at once
event.snakebite.treat.done: The wound is cut, cleaned and dressed. It will be painful for a while, but the worst has passed.
event.snakebite.rest: Keep them still and hope (a day)
event.snakebite.rest.done: You wait through a long day. The bite is serious.
event.frost_night.body: The night is bitterly cold. By midnight the water in the buckets is frozen, and frost glitters on the wagon tent.
event.frost_night.fires: Keep big fires going all night (half a day lost)
event.frost_night.fires.done: Everyone sleeps close to the fires and wakes stiff but warm enough.
event.frost_night.huddle.ok: It is a miserable night, but everyone gets through it.
event.frost_night.huddle.bad: By morning someone is shivering and cannot get warm.
event.griqua_riders.body: A party of Griqua horsemen rides up, armed and well mounted. Their leader greets you in Dutch and asks where you are bound.
event.griqua_riders.welcome.done: Over coffee they tell you about the road ahead and the grazing along it. They part from you as friends.
event.griqua_riders.trade.done: They have shot an eland. Tobacco changes hands, and you eat well tonight.
event.griqua_riders.wary: Keep your guns close and answer shortly
event.griqua_riders.wary.done: They notice your coldness and ride on without another word.
event.barolong_herders.body: Barolong herders are grazing cattle near the track. A young man comes over to see what you might trade.
event.barolong_herders.beads: Trade beads for meat and milk
event.barolong_herders.beads.done: The beads are looked over carefully and accepted. You get fresh meat and sour milk in return.
event.barolong_herders.tobacco.done: They grow their own tobacco now and are not much impressed with yours, but you agree on a bag of maize.
event.barolong_herders.greet.done: You exchange greetings and go your separate ways.
event.vegkop_survivor.body: You meet a trekker family whose wagons were in the laager at Vegkop last October. Their oxen are thin and borrowed, and almost all their sheep and cattle were driven off after the battle.
event.vegkop_survivor.listen: Sit with them and hear their story
event.vegkop_survivor.listen.done: They tell of the wagons lashed together, the long day of fighting, and the silence after. Their children listen as if they have heard it many times.
event.vegkop_survivor.share: Share some of your meal with them (half a muid)
event.vegkop_survivor.share.done: They accept the meal with tears in their eyes. Word of your kindness will travel among the trekkers.
event.retief_manifesto.body: At the evening halt a neighbour reads aloud from a copy of the Graham's Town Journal: Piet Retief's statement of why the families are leaving the Colony. The losses in the wars, the labour laws, the Government that does not protect them.
event.retief_manifesto.agree.done: Heads nod around the fire. The family feels part of something larger.
event.retief_manifesto.doubt: "Words are easy. We shall see what the north holds."
event.retief_manifesto.doubt.done: Someone mutters, but the talk moves on to oxen and grass.
event.governors_man.body: Trekkers stop at your wagon. One of them looks at you hard. "You are English. Did the Governor send you to keep an eye on us?"
event.governors_man.honest: Answer honestly, in the best Dutch you can
event.governors_man.honest.ok: They listen, and the hard faces soften a little. "Well, you speak our tongue at least."
event.governors_man.honest.cool: They hear you out, but they are not convinced. They ride on.
event.governors_man.angry: Tell them it is none of their business
event.governors_man.angry.done: Your words go round the camps quickly, and not to your credit.
event.stuck_wagon.body: A trekker wagon is stuck fast in a muddy stream bed, its oxen worn out. The family looks at your span hopefully.
event.stuck_wagon.help: Lend your oxen and help haul it out (half a day)
event.stuck_wagon.help.done: With your span added to theirs, the wagon comes free. The family thanks you warmly and promises not to forget it.
event.stuck_wagon.pass: Drive on; you cannot spare the oxen
event.stuck_wagon.pass.done: They watch you go by in silence.
